source_evidence: You should always consider your total cost of an investment, including sales charges, 12b-1 fees and other operating expenses.
answer: When comparing share classes of the same mutual fund, read the prospectus or prospectuses for each class and compare all the costs—not just the amount charged when you first invest. Include sales charges, ongoing 12b-1 fees, and other operating expenses. A class with lower initial fees may cost more over time, so consider how long you expect to hold the shares as well. If the fund describes its classes in separate prospectuses, review each one to understand the differences.
